summary: Tested multi-tab Google Sheet connect for India (admin) and Berlin (navya) plus the AiSensy 'Invalid Number' error rewrite. Backend pytest: 8/8 pass. It covers the tabs endpoint returning {tabs, title}, the 400 error for a bad URL, the auth check, multi-tab create storing spreadsheet_title, the 409 for a duplicate tab, account isolation for list and delete, editing via PUT, and delete. The unit test monkeypatches _send_whatsapp_api for berlin +49, berlin +968 and website 10-digit numbers; it confirms sent_to is the +intl number and the error is rewritten. In the UI, both accounts work: the title shows, all 5 tabs are listed, Select all / Clear all works, the count text and 'Connect N tabs & import' show, and send-existing and auto-sync are OFF by default. Saving creates one connection per tab and imports each one with WhatsApp queued 0. The group header reads 'VisaXpert Campaign Leads · 2 tabs connected' and the status reads '2 Google Sheets connected'. Connected tabs are disabled with a 'Connected' label, and Select all skips them. Edit mode is single-tab and saves a new tab and label. wa-error-text shows under the failed badge. One HIGH bug was found: the column mapping is left over from tabs that were deselected, so every Berlin lead was imported with no phone number.

minor.issue: Returns result.get('error') from _send_whatsapp_api, which is the raw AiSensy text "{'message': 'Invalid Number', 'name':'ERR400'}". The friendly message is only written to the DB. So the toast after a resend still shows the raw error, although the badge text is correct after reload. Fix: have send_routed_whatsapp return the rewritten error, or use the DB value.

Changing the gid/tab on a connection that has already synced keeps last_sync. The next Sync is then treated as a normal sync (send_messages=True), so it would send WhatsApp to every existing row of the new tab. The old tab's leads also stay attached. When the gid changes, the backend should reset last_sync (making it a first import) or refuse the change.

ui_bugs.issue: Reproduced as navya: Find tabs -> Select all (loads headers for all 5 tabs) -> Clear all -> pick EU and NON-EU. The mapping still holds 'phone_number' from the India tabs, but EU and NON-EU use the header 'phone'. As a result, all 129 Berlin leads were imported with an empty phone, and no WhatsApp could ever be sent or resent to them. Cause: loadHeaders only fills columns that are not yet mapped, and the mapping is never re-checked when picked tabs change. The <select> also keeps the stale value as an option, so the mismatch is hidden. The same happens when tabs with different headers (e.g. an India Meta form and a Berlin form) are picked together: one shared mapping is applied to all of them. Fix: recompute the guesses from the headers of the currently picked tabs (clear values not in `headers`). Warn or block when a mapped column (at least the phone column) is missing in any picked tab. Optionally, let the backend fall back to synonyms (phone/phone_number).

Each concurrent loadHeaders call (Select all) toggles the shared busy flag. The first call to finish re-enables Save while other headers are still loading, and the mapping can then be saved from a partial set of headers.

action_items: HIGH: Fix the stale column mapping in CampaignSheetModal. Re-guess the mapping from the picked tabs' headers when the selection changes, and validate that the phone column exists in every picked tab (EU/NON-EU use 'phone', the India forms use 'phone_number').
Make the resend endpoint return the rewritten friendly 'WhatsApp rejected +num ...' error to the toast.
When editing a synced connection to point at a different tab: reset last_sync or delete the old tab's leads, so the next Sync does not mass-message every existing row.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 5100+ lines; split the campaign-sheets and WhatsApp routing code into their own modules.
Auth uses email/password in query strings on every request, so credentials end up in logs and browser history.
In fetch_sheet_tabs, parsing the htmlview HTML with a regex is fragile; if Google changes that markup, tab discovery breaks.

success_rate.frontend: ~90% (all requested flows work; mapping bug causes Berlin phones to be empty)

seed_data_creation: None kept. Created 2 sheets per account via the UI (2 India tabs: 358 leads; EU and NON-EU for Berlin: 129 leads), plus TEST_ sheets via the API. Set whatsapp=failed on these test-created leads only, to render wa-error-text. Everything was removed afterwards via the UI Remove buttons. Final DB state: campaign_sheets=0, campaign_leads=0, whatsapp_messages=0. The temp DB wa_err_unit_tmp was dropped. No real WhatsApp was sent (every sync reported queued 0).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Spreadsheet tab gids: 99742259 (Centralized), 1798667875 (Pathankot copy) and 545121451 (Pathankot) use phone_number; 2139819490 (EU) and 1551110032 (NON-EU) use phone. To retest the mapping bug as navya: Select all -> Clear all -> pick EU and NON-EU, then check campaign-mapping-2 shows 'phone'. Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_multi_tab_and_wa_error.py -v (no network sends). Never re-sync an already-synced sheet and never click resend or 'Send all skipped'. Delete sheets afterwards.
rca of the issue: Mapping bug: SheetModal.loadHeaders runs setColumns(cols => cols.map(c => c.sheet_column ? c : guess)), so the first tab's headers that load win permanently. pickTab and pickAll never clear values that do not exist in the currently picked tabs' headers. The sync then looks up 'phone_number' in the EU/NON-EU CSV, finds nothing, gets values[2]='' and phone='', so the leads cannot be messaged.
